messages:
Morgan: heads up — noticed a p95 jump on hosted API around 10:04UTC, p95 went 180ms -> ~450ms, p99 into seconds. queue depth metric spiked at same time. rate-limiter drop counts went up too :thinking_face:
Priya: link to grafana?
Morgan: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/hosted-api?panel=p95 — the panel shows a sharp wave at 10:03:50, upstream requests steady.
Sam: checking runtime logs now. kselector emitted a bunch of kernel_fallback entries:
```
2023-11-02T10:03:52Z [kselector] model=gpt-small kernel=amx_v1 fallback=aux_kernel reason="incompatible_seq_len"
2023-11-02T10:03:53Z [kvcache] tenant=1009 evict=prefix count=120
```
Sam: also seeing coalescer delay bump: coalescer_delay_ms median -> 12ms to 60ms around same window.
Diego: tenant 1009? that's a known heavy short-seq tenant that recently flipped quantization profile. could be noisy neighbor.
Jen: do we have profiler traces for one of the slow requests?
Morgan: uploaded a pcap and a couple traces to the triage folder: s3://redwood-triage/1701234567/{trace-1.json,trace-2.json}
Priya: quick grep of scheduler logs shows queue_depth for host h-az3 spiked to 240 (normal 30-40). batching heuristic seems to have increased batch timeout to hit min_batch_size.
Sam: i pulled a runtime profile — inner loop shows increased time in copy_kv_cache and kernel selection path:
```
CPU  | time_ms
copy_kv_cache  | 42ms (was 8ms)
kselector_eval  | 37ms (was 5ms)
aux_kernel_launch | 120ms (spikes only during window)
```
Diego: copy_kv_cache 42ms suggests hot KV eviction thrash. maybe prefetch storm caused many misses and large mem copies.
Morgan: hypothesis: sudden influx of short-seq traffic from tenant 1009 triggered aggressive coalescing that increased queue depth, kselector mispredicted kernel (aux fallback) for short sequences after quantization change, and kvcache evictions caused heavy memcopy. combined -> p95/p99 spike.
Jen: can we validate by filtering host logs for tenant 1009 and comparing to baseline?
Sam: done. correlation is strong: requests from tenant 1009 accounted for 32% of requests in the spike window and 70% of kernel_fallback events.
Priya: mitigation options — 1) throttle tenant 1009 via rate-limiter; 2) pin their requests to aux-friendly kernel; 3) temporarily disable aggressive prefetch for that host; 4) increase kvcache capacity on affected hosts.
Diego: quick mitigation: add tenant 1009 to soft rate limit to shed traffic and reduce coalescer growth. can someone push a temporary policy? @infra-bot
infra-bot: acknowledged. applying soft-rate-limit tenant=1009 limit=20rps window=60s — will report back.
Morgan: started a canary rollback of their quantization profile to previous config for a subset of tokens (manual routing) — watch grafana for immediate delta.
Jen: i ran a dry-run of a kernel-selector tweak that biases toward main kernel when sequence_len <= 32; sim shows reduced fallback events by ~85% in the trace.
Sam: perf note — we should add a fast-path in copy_kv_cache for small prefix evictions (avoid full buffer memcpy). i can prototype a memcpy-bound check.
Priya: after infra-bot policy applied p95 dropped to ~220ms within 30s and queue depth started decaying. p99 still slightly elevated but trending down.
Diego: next steps:
- short: keep soft rate-limit for 30m and continue monitoring
- mid: implement kselector bias for <=32 seq and rollback quantization rollout for tenant 1009
- long: add fast-path for small kvcache copies + telemetry for prefetch miss rates per tenant
Sam: i'll open two PRs: kselector tweak (small) and kvcache memcpy opt (larger). link will be in the thread.
Jen: add an alert rule for kernel_fallback_rate > 0.1% over 5m per host so we catch this earlier.
Morgan: thanks all. filing an incident ticket and assigning follow-ups. attaching checklist:
```
- mitigate: soft rate-limit tenant 1009 (done)
- monitor: p95/p99, queue_depth, kvcache_evictions
- rollback: quantization rollout for tenant 1009 (partial rollback in flight)
- code: prototype kvcache memcpy opt, bias kselector for short seq
- postmortem: include traffic pattern, rollout timing, and remediation timeline
```
Priya: marking this thread for postmortem and assigning to eng-runtime oncall. :white_check_mark:
Morgan: closing live triage — will update incident ticket with timelines and links. good catch everyone. :rocket:
